title: Bounded Western local and monastic Eucharistic book states

traditions.label: Dominican use
traditions.scope: Latin missals of the Order of Preachers; the selected original Latin printings, not a translation history.
traditions.coverage_note: Page-collated states 1550, 1553, 1603 and 1604 bracket the Suscepimus Deus recombination. The 1985 postconciliar Proprium (Missal and Lectionary) is documented from its front matter as a supplement to the Roman Missal, which the Order was permitted to assume on 2 June 1969; the preconciliar 1933–1965 missals and the 1604–1985 interval are not staged.

traditions.label: Carmelite use
traditions.scope: Latin missals of the ancient observance of the Order of Carmel; not the Discalced Carmelites’ separate Roman-use books.
traditions.coverage_note: Two printings establish a bounded October calendar change. The precise intervening act is not yet identified. A confirmed 1972 general-council decree adopting the postconciliar Roman Missal (with a personal exception for older friars) marks the Order's change of book; it is an adoption event, not a stage.

traditions.label: Rite of Braga
traditions.scope: Bracarense Latin missals, kept distinct from Roman, Carmelite and Dominican uses.
traditions.coverage_note: 1538–1558 change is established through original scholarship. The 1924 approved state has direct prefatory evidence; its precise body revision remains open.

traditions.label: Carthusian use
traditions.scope: Carthusian Latin missals and the complementary Ordinarium; chapter and publication dates are distinguished.
traditions.coverage_note: The 1582 preparation and 1603 Gloria are reported through page-checked scholarship; the 1627 title and three Ordinary pages are directly image-checked. No complete-book reconstruction is asserted. An undated incunable missal (BSB-Ink [1496]; GW not after 1496) is recorded as a provisional stage; it prints the same oblation prayer, with word-order variants, and the same Gloria reading as 1561.

traditions.label: Sarum use
traditions.scope: Selected medieval Sarum missal witnesses, read through Legg’s critical edition.
traditions.coverage_note: Two manuscript states are distinguished without making their differences a single linear reform.

traditions.label: Hereford use
traditions.scope: The Whitchurch manuscript and the 1502 Hereford printing, through Henderson’s edition.
traditions.coverage_note: Local manuscript features and printed differences are documented; a diocesan revision mechanism is not established.

traditions.label: York use
traditions.scope: The early printed York sequence as compared by Henderson, with manuscript diversity retained as a limitation.
traditions.coverage_note: Five printed witnesses are not five demonstrated recensions.

traditions.label: Esztergom use
traditions.scope: The pre-1341 notated missal and 1484 Esztergom printing as compared in Déri’s critical edition.
traditions.coverage_note: Substantive repertory differences are established by scholarship; the exact sequence of intermediate revisions is not.

sources.title: Notitiae 5 (1969), no. 48, pp. 359–360: Order of Preachers, 2 June 1969 (Prot. n. 98/69), Roman Missal and calendar
sources.inspection: Page images of printed pp. 359–360 (PDF 33–34) viewed 2026-10-22 from a prior-lane copy of the whole issue (SHA-256 f31becd3…). Under section III (Decreta circa ritus et calendaria particularia) the Order of Preachers is granted, for the whole Order, the restored Missale Romanum of Paul VI and the Universal Norms with the new General Roman Calendar and Litany; after adoption the Master General (for the Order) or a provincial (for his subjects) may license priests to celebrate according to the Dominican rite then in force; until a definitive Order calendar is approved, first-class Dominican feasts (Rosary, Dominic, Thomas Aquinas, Catherine of Siena) become solemnities, second-class feasts become feasts, third-class saints obligatory memorials and the rest optional memorials. A following paragraph gives pastoral reasons and the difficulty of printing proper books for this and a Cistercian request.
sources.limitations: Published decree summary, not the signed rescript or its ASOP 39 (1969) pp. 250–251 printing. It grants permission; it does not date the Order's actual changeover or any house's licensed continuation of the Dominican rite.

sources.title: Notitiae 8 (1972), no. 69, pp. 14 and 17–18: Dominican chapter decree confirmed (1971) and A. Dirks, De ritu dominicano
sources.inspection: Page images of printed pp. 14, 17 and 18 (PDF 20, 27–28) viewed 2026-10-22 (copy SHA-256 0ccd64a2…). P. 14: 7 October 1971 (Prot. n. 1725/71) confirmation of the general chapters' (1968, 1971) decree adopting the restored Office for the whole Dominican family. Pp. 17–18: Ansgarius Dirks OP states that the 1968 general chapter decreed adoption of the restored Roman rite, cites the 1969 concession at Notitiae 5 (1969) p. 359, and gives as examples the Dominican offertory (bread and wine offered together with the single prayer Suscipe sancta Trinitas) and the shorter Dominican Confiteor.
sources.limitations: An official-journal commentary by a Dominican, not the chapter acts; the Office decree concerns the Liturgy of the Hours. The examples describe the former rite in general terms, not a collation of named editions.

stages.label: Venice witness before the Xavierre revision
stages.scope: Suscepimus Deus formulary within the temporale.
stages.witness_label: Missale ad usum fratrum Praedicatorum Sancti Dominici, Venice, 1550
stages.summary: Suscepimus Deus appears under Dominica octava, with Deus cuius providentia as collect and Attendite a falsis prophetis as Gospel.

evidence.claim: Venice 1550 is printed on the title.
The named formulary and texts are visible on the identified folios.

stages.limitations: This does not reconstruct the full 1550 missal, identify its immediate exemplar, or establish how long each house used it.
stages.reception: The title identifies the Dominican use. A printed intended-use statement does not prove reception in every province.

stages.label: Venice printing of the Salamanca 1551 chapter reform
stages.scope: Title declaration of the 1551 chapter reform and the Suscepimus Deus formulary within the temporale.
stages.witness_label: Missale secundum ordinem fratrum Praedicatorum, Venice: Giunta, 1553; BSB
stages.summary: The title declares the missal reformed according to the decrees of the general chapter held at Salamanca in 1551 and apostolically approved. Suscepimus Deus is headed Dominica septima (counted post octavam Trinitatis under the fol. 114r renumbering rubric) and keeps the collect Deus cuius providentia, the epistle Debitores sumus and the Gospel Attendite a falsis prophetis.

evidence.claim: Iuxta decreta Capituli Generalis anno Domini 1551 Salmanticae celebrati reformatum, authoritate Apostolica comprobatum; Venetiis apud Iuntas MDLIII.

Introit Suscepimus Deus; collect Deus cuius providentia; Romans 8 Debitores sumus; Matthew 7 Attendite a falsis prophetis; the preceding Mass ends with the same Sicut in holocausto offertory as in 1550.

stages.limitations: A single formulary is checked. The book's title claims a chapter reform but this does not show which components the 1551 chapter changed.
stages.reception: A printed missal for the Order; reception in particular provinces is not established.

stages.label: Rome 1603 printing of the Xavierre revision
stages.scope: Title, prefatory instruments and the Suscepimus Deus formulary.
stages.witness_label: Missale iuxta ritum sacri ordinis Praedicatorum, Rome: Ciacconi apud Vulliettum, 1603; BSB
stages.summary: Already in 1603 Suscepimus Deus stands under Dominica sexta post octavas Trinitatis with the collect Largire nobis, the epistle Debitores sumus and the unjust-steward Gospel of Luke 16, as in the 1604 printing.

evidence.claim: Sub Hieronymo Xavierre recognitum et emendatum, apostolic approval; Romae, in officina Alfonsi Ciacconi, apud Carolum Vulliettum, MDCIII.
Dominica sexta: introit Suscepimus Deus; collect Largire nobis quaesumus Domine semper spiritum cogitandi; Romans 8 Debitores sumus; Luke 16 Homo quidam erat dives qui habebat villicum.

stages.limitations: One formulary; the 1603 and 1604 printings are different settings, so this records the earlier attested date of the revised combination, not the first printing.
stages.reception: The same Xavierre revision as the 1604 stage; local uptake is not established.

stages.label: Xavierre revision witnessed in the Rome printing
stages.scope: A revised temporale formulary and the revision’s reprinted authorizing documents.
stages.witness_label: Missale juxta ritum sacri ordinis Praedicatorum S. P. N. Dominici, Rome, ex typographia Alfonsi Ciacconi, apud Carolum Vulliettum, 1604
stages.summary: Suscepimus Deus now has Largire nobis as collect and the unjust-steward Gospel, with its heading moved to Dominica sexta after the octave of Trinity.

evidence.claim: Printing dated 1604, under Hieronymus Xavierre.
The editor explicitly describes conformity of Epistles and Gospels to Roman use.
The revised combination is directly visible.

stages.limitations: The original intervention predates this printing; 1604 is not assigned as the first promulgation or first revised edition. Only the selected formulary is text-collated.
stages.reception: Clement VIII’s brief dated 2 April 1602 preserves the Order’s rite while authorizing conformity in specified matters. Its adoption windows depend on place and availability of copies; actual local uptake is not established.

stages.label: Carmelite October calendar before the later additions
stages.scope: Printed October calendar.
stages.witness_label: Missale antique professionis Regularium beatissime Dei genitricis semperque virginis Marie de Monte Carmelo, Venice: Giunta, 1574
stages.summary: October 5 has no printed feast. October 6 includes Abraham, Isaac and Jacob with three lessons and the octave of Michael; October 8 includes Simeon the prophet.

evidence.claim: Imprint is Venice, Giunta, 1574; the book identifies the Carmelite observance and custom of Jerusalem.
These printed entries are directly visible.

stages.limitations: Calendar absence on one date is not proof that a saint or devotion is absent from every section of the volume.
stages.reception: This is the Carmelite Latin book identified by its own title. The title’s Jerusalem claim is recorded without constructing a genealogy from it.

stages.label: Carmelite calendar with Teresa of Jesus
stages.scope: Printed October calendar and Teresa’s printed common-Mass reference.
stages.witness_label: Missale fratrum Carmelitarum Ordinis Beatae Dei Genitricis Mariae de monte Carmelo, Venice: Giunta, 1621
stages.summary: October 5 prints Teresa as duplex minus with a commemoration of Placidus and companions. Teresa’s sanctoral entry directs the reader to the common Dilexisti iustitiam Mass.

evidence.claim: The 1621 printing is described as printed again, with chapter and Prior General authority.
Teresa’s feast and common-Mass reference are printed, distinct from marginal handwriting.
The instrument is dated 26 September 1584, not 1621.

stages.limitations: Neither the exact introduction date of Teresa’s feast nor the date of the chapter decree is established. Manuscript corrections in this copy are excluded.
stages.reception: The printed book belongs to the Carmelite ancient-observance sequence. A handwritten direction to a Discalced missal on p. 409 is not treated as the printed rite’s prescription.

stages.label: Galharde’s revised Braga printing before Limpo
stages.scope: Directly inspected Palm Sunday blessing and the printing’s own account of corrections and additions.
stages.witness_label: Missale Bracarense, Lisbon: Germão Galharde, 1538; BNP RES-1633-A
stages.summary: The colophon reports corrected passages, added Gloria/Credo rules and Masses of Christian victory and St Apollonia, preface notation following Coimbra cathedral practice, and removal of some material already available in the Manual. The Palm blessing has seven prayers and one preface.

evidence.claim: Identifies the 1538 witness.
Colophon and comparison identify this state.

evidence.locus: Colophon fol. 184v, PDF 364; preceding recto foliation on PDF 363
evidence.claim: The colophon dates publication decimo septimo kalendas Augusti 1538 (16 July); names Galharde and corrector Fernandus Olegarius; expressly lists corrections, additions and omissions.

Seven prayer units are visible: Omnipotens…in diluvio, Petimus te, Deus cuius filius, Deus qui dispersa congregas, Domine Iesu Christe, Benedic Domine hos ramos, Omnipotens Iesu Christe; the preface begins Qui miro dispositionis ordine.

stages.limitations: The 1538 colophon describes its own revision without identifying the exact previous printing as an immediate parent. The earlier state has not been directly collated. This surviving copy is incomplete; the whole digital file is acquired, not the complete original printed volume.
stages.reception: A book of the church of Braga; surviving print identification does not establish continuous archdiocesan use until 1558.

stages.label: Limpo’s revised Braga missal
stages.scope: Reported changes to the Ordo and Palm Sunday blessing.
stages.witness_label: Missale juxta usum et ordinem Almae Bracarensis Ecclesiae, Lyon: Petrus Fradin, 1558; BnF B-1478
stages.summary: Limpo’s revision changes the Ordo and Palm Sunday blessing.

evidence.claim: Identifies the 1558 witness.
Describes concrete revisions.

stages.limitations: Primary leaves were not reached; no word-for-word collation is claimed.
stages.reception: Revision for Braga. Limpo’s Carmelite membership does not establish derivation from a Carmelite missal; Carvalho rejects direct dependence on the Carmelite 1551 and Lyon 1556 books he compared.

stages.label: Braga typical edition approved in December 1924
stages.scope: The title edition and its binding approval/conformity rules; no complete body reconstruction. Batch 4 adds directly inspected 1924 body loci: the Palm Sunday blessing, the Sacred Heart and Assumption Masses and the end-of-October sequence.
stages.witness_label: Missale Bracarense, Rome: Typis Polyglottis Vaticanis, 1924; title edition distinct from the digitized copy’s later supplements
stages.summary: Approved 8 December and declared typical 9 December 1924. Future Holy See changes to Masses already contained in it must be applied; newly imposed universal feasts must enter the Braga calendar. The 1924 body prints the Palm blessing with five prayers before the preface Qui gloriaris in consilio sanctorum and Haec tibi Domine festa recoluntur after the Sanctus; the Sacred Heart Mass Egredimini with the preface of the Cross; and the Assumption Mass Gaudeamus. Its index of feasts names local feasts such as the consecration of the archdiocese to the Sacred Heart (16 May) and the coronation of the Immaculate of Sameiro (12 June).

evidence.claim: Identifies the revised 1924 Vatican printing.
The dateline is 8 December 1924; it directs the archdiocese’s priests to this missal.
The decree dated 9 December 1924 declares the edition typical and sets the future conformity and feast-insertion rules.

Prayers Deus cujus Filius; Omnipotens Jesu Christe mundi Creator; Omnipotens sempiterne Deus qui in diluvio; Bone Redemptor Domine; Deus qui dispersa congregas; preface Qui gloriaris in consilio sanctorum tuorum with Sanctus; then Haec tibi Domine festa recoluntur.
Sacred Heart Mass with Introit Egredimini (Cant. 3, 11) and the direction Praefatio de Cruce, in the body pagination.
Assumption Mass with Introit Gaudeamus and collect Veneranda nobis, in the body pagination.

Lists the consecration of the archdiocese to the Sacred Heart (16 May, p. 599) and the coronation of the Immaculate of Monte Sameiro (12 June, p. 623, PDF 775) among feasts of the Lord and of the Virgin.

stages.limitations: These rules describe the 1924 state; their absence from 1558 has not been established. Later inserted feasts in this copy must not be assigned to 1924. The batch-4 inspection does not show which 1924 contents were new in 1924: the 1558 book was not reached, so the Palm blessing agreement with Bragança's 1558 count and the presence of modern feasts are recorded as 1924 contents, not as 1924 changes.
stages.reception: The bull requires this missal for priests of the Archdiocese of Braga. This establishes the contemporary prescription, not universal subsequent observance or present law.

stages.label: Braga 1924 altar copy with bound supplements to 1961
stages.date_label: After 21 November 1961 (latest dated supplement leaf) and before the copy's digitization (Internet Archive item added 1 February 2026); 1924 body
stages.scope: One digitized altar copy of the 1924 Braga missal into which supplement leaves with their own Rites concordats or Braga imprimaturs were bound; selected propers and the insert sequence only.
stages.witness_label: Missale Bracarense 1924 working copy with supplements, Internet Archive missale-bracarense-1924 (PDF SHA-256 2be6474d…0841)
stages.summary: Twenty-one inserts supply later Masses for this Braga altar book: the 1929 Sacred Heart Mass Cogitationes with its own preface, Christ the King (Turin 1927), the Assumption Mass Signum magnum (Braga 16 December 1950), the Common of Supreme Pontiffs (1942/1947), the votive Mass of Christ the Eternal High Priest (1935/1936) and saints from Teresa of the Child Jesus (1925/1928) to Gregory Barbarigo and Anthony Mary Claret as third-class feasts (Braga 21 November 1961).

evidence.claim: Sacred Heart Mass with Introit Cogitationes (Ps. 32) and Sacred Heart preface in solemn, ferial and spoken forms; Rites concordat dated 2 April 1929.
Assumption Mass with Introit Signum magnum (Apoc. 12); Braga imprimatur dated 16 December 1950.

evidence.locus: Insert PDF 964–971, between printed pp. 796 (PDF 963) and 797 (PDF 972)
evidence.claim: Mass of Christ the King for the last Sunday of October with chant preface; concordat Turin 7 April 1927; Marietti 1927 imprint.

evidence.locus: Single insert PDF 781, after printed p. 628
evidence.claim: Gregory Barbarigo (17 June) and Anthony Mary Claret (23 October), each headed 3. classis; Braga imprimatur 21 November 1961, the latest dated leaf found.

Further saints' Masses, the Common of Supreme Pontiffs and the Eternal High Priest votive Mass, each with its own concordat or imprimatur dated between 1925 and 1959 (e.g. Teresa of the Child Jesus: Rites 17 May 1925, Braga 3 October 1928; John Bosco: Turin 6 May 1936, Braga 5 August 1936).

stages.limitations: A physical copy's accretion, not a new edition: the supplements are separately approved leaves bound into a 1924 book, and the scan's order reflects binding and uploader assembly. The body pages still print the superseded 1924 formularies. The copy does not prove when any church adopted each supplement, and absence of a later leaf from this copy proves nothing about its issue. Some approbation dates were read from low-resolution images.
stages.reception: The inserts carry their own approbations: Sacred Congregation of Rites concordats, Turin archdiocesan concordats or imprimaturs, and Braga archiepiscopal imprimaturs. Not every leaf carries Braga approval: the Christ the King leaf has only a Turin concordat and imprimatur (7 April 1927) with a Marietti imprint, and the final page of the 1929 Sacred Heart leaf has only the Rites concordat. Binding into this Braga altar copy shows they were supplied for use with it; actual use in a named church is not established.

stages.label: Early printed Carthusian missal with a brief Ordinary block before the Canon
stages.date_label: [1496] as attributed by BSB-Ink M-423 (GW M24135: not after 1496); no printed date in the edition or the inspected copy
stages.scope: The Ordinary block before the Canon (oblation prayer, Gloria, Creed, prefaces) in an incunable Carthusian missal.
stages.witness_label: Missale Cartusiense, [Speyer, about 1496], BSB bsb00030081
stages.summary: Before the Canon the book prints the oblation prayer In spiritu humilitatis, closing with In nomine Patris et Filii et Spiritus sancti, without accompanying rubric, followed by the Gloria (propter gloriam tuam magnam), the Creed and the prefaces.

evidence.locus: BSB canvases 231–234 (printed folio xxix and following)
evidence.claim: Oblation, Gloria, Creed and prefaces read from the page images.

evidence.locus: BSB manifest metadata (2 Inc.s.a. 879); BSB-Ink M-423; GW M24135; canvases 1–11 and 560–572
evidence.claim: Bracketed attribution [Speyer, Peter Drach the younger for Henrick Eckert van Homberch, 1496] (BSB-Ink); GW gives 'not after 1496'. The text ends on canvas 560 (fol. 263v) without a colophon; canvases 561–570 are blank.

stages.limitations: Provisional (cold review 2026-10-22): the year is a catalogue attribution, not read in the book, and the catalogues differ in precision (BSB-Ink [1496]; GW not after 1496); the inspected block shows no textual difference from Pavia 1561 that is encoded as a change. The year is a catalogue attribution, not read in the book. Only the block before the Canon was read; the water prayer, incensation and Orate fratres were not found on canvases 230–234, which bounds a search of this block, not of the whole book. A complementary Ordinarium may have carried such rubrics.
stages.reception: Printed for the Delft bookseller Eckert van Homberch; ownership and use in a named charterhouse are not established.

stages.label: Pavia charterhouse printing licensed by the Prior General
stages.scope: Licence, colophon and selected Ordinary loci.
stages.witness_label: Missale Carthusiense, printed in the charterhouse of Pavia, 1561; BSB
stages.summary: The patent of Frater Petrus, Prior of the Grande Chartreuse and Minister General, dated at the Grande Chartreuse 28 August 1560 under the General Chapter's authority, licenses the Pavia charterhouse to print the Order's missals and other books in the same form as the editions of Thielman Kerver of Paris (now sold out), the large missals first printed at Lyon being also exhausted, and forbids other printings without licence. The Gloria reads propter gloriam tuam magnam; the water prayer is De latere Domini nostri Iesu Christi; the chalice offering is In spiritu humilitatis; and the Orate asks prayer pro me peccatore.

evidence.claim: Licence of Frater Petrus, Prior of the Grande Chartreuse, dated 28 August 1560, countersigned by the chapter scribe Laurentius Reboleti.
In Cartusia Papie ... 1561, die vigesimo octavo Septembris.
Gloria, Credo and offertory/Orate texts and rubrics read from the images.

stages.limitations: The licence asserts reproduction of an existing form, not revision; whether the text differs from the Kerver or Lyon printings is not examined.
stages.reception: Licensed by the Prior General for the Order's use; reception in particular charterhouses is not established.

stages.label: Carthusian preparation in the 1582 Ordinarium
stages.scope: Reported preparatory prayers and gestures in the complementary Ordinarium.
stages.witness_label: Ordinarium Cartusiense, Paris, 1582
stages.summary: Preparation begins at the Gospel side with Pone Domine and a short Confiteor; the confession includes omissione and three strikes of the breast.

evidence.claim: Describes the preparation from the Ordinarium and states that the 1603 missal does not print these preparation texts.

stages.limitations: Primary leaves not directly inspected. Their omission from a missal is not treated as omission from the liturgy or a ritual revision.
stages.reception: An identified order-level prescription or scholarly description does not establish use in every charterhouse.

stages.label: Paris missal following the 1602 chapter
stages.scope: Reported Gloria wording and title authority.
stages.witness_label: Missale Cartusiani Ordinis, Paris: Iametius Mettayer, 1603
stages.summary: The Gloria reads propter gloriam tuam magnam. The cited title invokes the general chapter held in 1602; 1603 is the publication year.

evidence.claim: Prints the Gloria word order and title with chapter 1602 and imprint 1603.

stages.limitations: USUARIUM 8356 links Google Books UxFlAAAAcAAJ, whose complete download returned HTTP 429. The 1582 Ordinarium is complementary evidence, not a demonstrated parent version.
stages.reception: An identified order-level prescription or scholarly description does not establish use in every charterhouse.

stages.label: Lyon witness authorized by the 1622 chapter
stages.scope: Title and printed Ordinary prayers on pp. 203–205.
stages.witness_label: Missale Cartusiani Ordinis, Lyon: Ioannes Pillehotte, 1627; BSB 2 Liturg. 197
stages.summary: The title invokes the chapter of 1622. Gloria retains propter gloriam tuam magnam; the water prayer begins De latere Domini, the chalice offering uses In spiritu humilitatis, and Orate asks prayer pro me peccatore.

evidence.claim: Chapter year 1622 and Lyon printing 1627 are explicit.
The named Ordinary prayer loci and rubrics are directly image-checked.

stages.limitations: The legacy cartusiense-1620 identifier remains for stable references only. No complete Ordinary transcription and no intervening change from 1603 is inferred.
stages.reception: An identified order-level prescription or scholarly description does not establish use in every charterhouse.

stages.label: Postconciliar Carthusian proper calendar confirmed in 2018, printed in the 2021 missal
stages.scope: The Order's proper calendar as confirmed on 30 November 2018 and printed in the 2021 missal; no prayer text. The 2021 Praenotanda are reported as that book's own description, not as part of the 2018 approval.
stages.witness_label: Missale Cartusiense 2021 (unofficially hosted PDF) and Notitiae 2018 record
stages.summary: The Congregation for Divine Worship confirmed the Carthusian proper calendar on 30 November 2018 (Prot. 156/18), and the 2021 missal prints that approval at the head of its calendar. The calendar Prooemium says it revises the Kalendarium perpetuum approved by the Congregation of Rites on 28 February 1917. The 2021 book's Praenotanda n. 2, whose own approval date is unknown, lists the restored missal's distinctive features: more prefaces and formularies taken from the Roman Missal, Communion under both kinds, conventual concelebration, a universal prayer on Sundays and solemnities, an enlarged body of orations, more Commons, revised votive Masses and some vernacular use.

evidence.claim: Ordinis Cartusiensis: Calendarium proprium (30 nov. 2018; Prot. 156/18).
Approval line: Congregation for Divine Worship, 30 November 2018, Prot. N 156/18.
Lists the distinctive features (a)-(h) of the restored missal.
Names the 1917 Kalendarium perpetuum as the revised base.

stages.limitations: The approval date belongs to the calendar, not to the whole missal; the missal's own recognition date and the reported 1981 printing remain unestablished. The 2021 PDF is unofficially hosted.
stages.reception: Approved by the Holy See for the Order; Praenotanda n. 15 adds house calendars, so observance varies by charterhouse.

stages.label: Crawford missal before the later vesting additions
stages.scope: The base Ordinary and calendar of Legg’s manuscript C.
stages.witness_label: Sarum Missal, John Rylands Library Latin MS 24; Legg manuscript C
stages.summary: Veni Creator belongs at the beginning of Mass. The relics feast is entered on 15 September and Corpus Christi is absent from the base book. Prayers for individual vestments in a vacant space are a much later hand.

evidence.claim: Dates and identifies Latin MS 24 as a mid-thirteenth-century Salisbury manuscript.
Identifies C and distinguishes its base Ordinary/calendar from late additions.

stages.limitations: The numeric bounds encode the identified century, not a claim of use throughout it. No universal Sarum inception date is inferred, and later added prayers are not dated to the base hand.
stages.reception: A Sarum book, with Legg recording its own closing identification of the use; no claim that every Sarum church used an identical Ordinary.

stages.label: Bologna manuscript’s vesting and offertory arrangement
stages.date_label: First quarter of the fourteenth century
stages.scope: The Ordinary in Legg’s manuscript B, with added calendar directions kept distinct.
stages.witness_label: Sarum Missal, Bologna University Library MS 2565; Legg manuscript B
stages.summary: Individual vestment prayers accompany preparation, while Veni Creator occurs at the offertory. A later calendar annotation directs the relics feast to the Sunday after the July translation of Thomas of Canterbury, while its service remains at the September position.

evidence.claim: Identifies and dates B; distinguishes the later calendar annotation and describes the Ordinary difference.

stages.limitations: The annotation is later than the base hand and has no independently verified insertion date. C and B are compared witnesses, not a demonstrated immediate parent and revised child.
stages.reception: The editor suggests an Oxford destination from a Frideswide formulary; this remains his inference, not a new provenance finding.

stages.label: Whitchurch manuscript with local Dubricius observance
stages.scope: Selected calendar and Mass proper features in Henderson’s University College manuscript.
stages.witness_label: Hereford-use Whitchurch missal, University College Oxford; Henderson’s fourteenth-century manuscript
stages.summary: The calendar marks the local dedication on 11 March and Dubricius on 14 November; a Dubricius Mass is present. For the second Sunday of Lent Henderson reports the Secret Sacrificiis praesentibus, Domine.

evidence.claim: Identifies the manuscript, local dedication and Dubricius Mass, and prints its second-Lent-Sunday Secret variant.

stages.limitations: The manuscript is incomplete, including substantial Holy Week and Canon losses. The feast’s presence in a local book does not prove that it was obligatory across the diocese.
stages.reception: Henderson identifies the original church as Whitchurch, Monmouthshire, from its dedication to Dubricius.

stages.label: Hereford printing represented by Henderson
stages.scope: Selected proper differences from the Whitchurch manuscript.
stages.witness_label: Missale Herfordense, Rouen: Pierre Olivier and Jean Mauditier for Jean Richard, 1502; represented by Henderson 1874
stages.summary: The printed second-Sunday-of-Lent Secret is Ecclesiae tuae, Domine, munera placatus assume. Henderson reports that the manuscript’s Dubricius Mass is absent from the printing.

evidence.claim: Transcribes the 1 September 1502 imprint and episcopal/chapter authority claim.
Reports the Dubricius difference and allows the manuscript Secret to be compared with the printed base text.

stages.limitations: The 1502 original is mediated by Henderson’s critical reprint. The witness difference does not identify when or why the prayers diverged, nor prove a diocesan decree removing a local feast.
stages.reception: The printed title reports bishop, dean and chapter authority; geographical uptake remains unestablished.

stages.label: York’s closely related printed witnesses
stages.scope: Henderson’s bounded comparison of five printed editions.
stages.witness_label: York missals: Violette, undated c. 1509; Gachet 1516; Bernard/Cousin 1517; Gachet 1530; Regnault 1533
stages.summary: The earliest printing lacks the monthly calendar notices and places Modus finiendi Collectas and Considerationes circa Missam differently. Henderson reports shared errors across the sequence, including an omitted Holy Saturday rubric line and Petrocius placed in April rather than June; musical note lengths also vary.

evidence.claim: Lists the early prints and describes their limited differences and continuing shared errors.

stages.limitations: This bounded witness group is not one complete reconstructed book or five independently proved recensions. The first print is undated; c. 1509 is the editor’s attribution. His proposed manuscript ancestry is explicitly tentative.
stages.reception: Printed intended use is York. Henderson describes substantial earlier manuscript ceremonial diversity, so the printed state must not be projected backwards to all medieval York books.

stages.label: Notated missal’s larger medieval repertory
stages.scope: Preparation placement and proper/sequence repertory compared by Déri with 1484.
stages.witness_label: Missale notatum Strigoniense ante 1341; main volume AM Bratislava EC Lad 3, with related surviving material
stages.summary: Déri counts approximately 210 saints with special propers and 78 sequences in the fourteenth-century notated missal. It also includes the Pentecost-octave Mass and the Transfiguration grape blessing that his later comparators lack. Preparation follows the Holy Saturday baptismal order.

evidence.claim: Identifies the main volume and dates the witness 1320–1341.
States the earlier repertory and compares it with the fifteenth-century witnesses.

stages.limitations: The manuscript is incomplete and composite surviving material must be mapped carefully. Its fuller repertory may include options rather than mandatory observance of every listed item.
stages.reception: A medieval Esztergom exemplar; no claim that every listed saint or sequence was used in every celebration.

stages.label: Esztergom’s 1484 printed repertory
stages.scope: Selected repertory and arrangement changes reported in Déri’s edition.
stages.witness_label: Missale Strigoniense, Nuremberg: Anton Koberger, completed 31 August 1484; Déri’s critical text
stages.summary: Compared with the pre-1341 witness, the special-proper sanctoral is reduced by about one third. The later sequentiary retains 39 of the earlier 78 sequences and adds ten others; its material substantially agrees with the intervening Pálóczi manuscript. Preparation prayers move to the beginning of the book.

evidence.claim: Reproduces the 31 August 1484 colophon, printer and chapter/vicar authority.
Describes preparation placement, sanctoral reduction and sequence comparison.

stages.limitations: The 1484 book is not identified as the moment when all differences first arose. Déri expressly requires more complex relationships than a single subtraction/addition sequence; the Pálóczi comparator already shares much of the later state. The absent intervening preparation texts could be a copying omission or assumed memorized text, not a proven ritual abolition.
stages.reception: The colophon identifies Esztergom use and the vicar and chapter’s assent; survival of a printing does not demonstrate uniform implementation.

stages.label: 1985 Dominican Proprium: Missal and Lectionary as a supplement to the Roman Missal
stages.date_label: Rome, ad Sanctae Sabinae, 1985; promulgation letter of Master Vincent de Couesnongle dated 15 August 1983; printing mandate of Master Damian Byrne, 3 April 1985 (Prot. 50/85/310)
stages.scope: The Order's postconciliar proper for Mass in one typical volume: ritual elements of the proper of time, the proper of saints, the lectionary of saints and chant indications, for use with the restored Roman Missal. It is not a complete independent Dominican Missal.
stages.witness_label: Proprium Ordinis Praedicatorum: Missale et Lectionarium, editio typica, Rome 1985 (order-hosted facsimile)
stages.summary: The 1968 River Forest chapter decided to adopt the restored Roman rite, and on 2 June 1969 the Order received leave to assume the restored Roman Missal and calendar. Master Vincent de Couesnongle promulgated this Missal and Lectionary of the Order's proper and declared the Latin edition typical by a letter dated 15 August 1983; Master Damian Byrne ordered it printed on 3 April 1985, and it was published in 1985. Its front matter prints the confirmations of the retained peculiar elements (1977), the Latin proper and lectionary texts (1978) and the Masses of the Order's Blessed (1980).

evidence.locus: Title PDF 1; mandate PDF 2 (3 April 1985, Prot. 50/85/310)
evidence.claim: Typical edition of the Order's Missale et Lectionarium, printed at Santa Sabina in 1985 and made the norm for vernacular editions.

CD 671/76 (25 July 1977) allows the Order's peculiar elements ad libitum; CD 1590/77 (18 February 1978) confirms the Latin Proprium Missarum and lectionary texts; CD 998/80 (7 November 1980) confirms the Latin Masses of the Order's Blessed; later grants follow.

evidence.locus: Promulgation letter nn. 3–5 and note 5, printed pp. X–XI (PDF 8–9)
evidence.claim: The 1968 chapter sought adoption of the restored Roman rite, the Roman Missal and then the new Roman Order of Mass were adopted, and the volume is presented as a supplement to the Roman Missal; note 5 cites CD 98/69 of 2 June 1969.

evidence.locus: Promulgation letter n. 23 and dating clause, printed pp. XVIII–XIX (PDF 16–17)
evidence.claim: Couesnongle promulgates the Missal and Lectionary for the whole Order and declares the Latin edition typical; the letter is dated Rome, Santa Sabina, 15 August 1983, before the 1985 printing mandate.
The Congregation's 2 June 1969 concession of the Roman Missal and calendar to the whole Order, with licences for the former rite and interim feast grades.
Confirmation of the chapter decree on the Office and Dirks's account of the 1968 decision to adopt the Roman rite.

stages.limitations: Only the front matter and promulgation letter were read; the body is not collated against the 1604 printing or the 1933, 1939 and 1965 Dominican missals, so no transition is drawn from any earlier Dominican stage. The 1969 Roman adoption and interim calendar, the 1971 Office confirmation and the 1983 promulgation are recorded as evidence here, not as separate book states; the stage date is the 1985 publication.
stages.reception: The 1969 concession allowed superiors to license priests to keep the Dominican rite then in force; the date of each house's changeover and any licensed continuation are not evidenced. The 1985 mandate directs vernacular editions to conform to this typical edition; actual use of the Latin volume in named houses is not established.

transitions.summary: Under the Sunday-numbering reform printed in the 1553 book (fol. 114r rubric, dated to the 1552 missal and breviary revision under the Salamanca chapter decrees), the Sunday after Trinity is renamed Dominica infra octavam Corporis Christi and the following Sundays are numbered post octavam Trinitatis. The Suscepimus Deus formulary therefore passes from the heading Dominica octava (post festum Trinitatis) to Dominica septima on the same Sunday. Collect, epistle and Gospel are unchanged.

changes.before: Heading Dominica octava in a series counted from the Sunday after Trinity, headed Dominica prima post festum Trinitatis (fol. 120v).
changes.after: Heading Dominica septima in the series renumbered post octavam Trinitatis by the fol. 114r rubric; the Sunday after Trinity is now Dominica infra octavam Corporis Christi (fol. 113r). The formulary still falls on the eighth Sunday after Trinity Sunday.

evidence.claim: Headings read from the page images: Dominica prima post festum Trinitatis and Dominica octava (Suscepimus Deus).
Reform rubric and headings read from the page images; the printed running heads are hand-altered and inconsistent and are not used.
Earlier formulary.
Later formulary with unchanged collect Deus cuius providentia and Gospel Attendite.
Rubric enacting the 1552 renaming and renumbering under the Salamanca chapter decrees.

The rubric also states that the renamed Sunday's Gospel changed. The cold reviewer saw 1550 fol. 121r (Luke 16, Homo quidam erat dives et induebatur purpura) and 1553 fol. 113v (John 6, Ego sum panis vitae), but this is not encoded as a change here. No immediate parent-child printing relation is asserted.

transitions.summary: Between 1553 and 1603 the Suscepimus Deus formulary receives the collect Largire nobis and the unjust-steward Gospel, and its Sunday is renamed in the post-octave count.

evidence.claim: Collect read from the page image.
Collect read from the page image.

changes.after: Gospel Luke 16, Homo quidam erat dives qui habebat villicum.

evidence.claim: Gospel read from the page image.
Gospel read from the page image.

evidence.claim: Heading series and the Sunday within the Corpus Christi octave read from the page images.
Heading series and the Sunday within the Corpus Christi octave read from the page images.
Earlier formulary.
